summary: BBN's host status report for February 14 to 25, 1972, noting that MIT-AI became a network user. It was replaced by RFC 319.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 315 reports ARPANET host status from February 14 to February 25, 1972, and says MIT-AI became a network user during that period. It includes daily test results and operator predictions, and RFC 319 later replaced it.

subtitle: A February 1972 snapshot of ARPANET host status and service predictions

tldr.problem: Network users needed a record of host accessibility and which machines could provide services to other sites.
tldr.mechanism: The report lists hosts excluded from testing, operator-reported status or predictions, and daily test results for the period.
tldr.outcome: It records MIT-AI's change to a network user and was later replaced by RFC 319.

sections.title: The Reporting Period
sections.content:
The report covers most Network Hosts from February 14 through February 25. It notes that MIT-AI's PDP-10, network address 134, became a Network User during those two weeks.

The report identifies hosts not expected to function as servers regularly for at least two weeks and hosts intended only as users. It then summarizes host status in tables.
sections.plainLanguage: This report covers most hosts for the listed period. It notes that MIT-AI became a network user and explains which machines were not included in daily tests.

sections.title: Tests and Status Codes
sections.content:
The table lists test results at the dates and Eastern times shown. O means a host opened a connection and was accessible to users. D means it was dead or inaccessible from the BBN Terminal IMP; H means it opened a connection but immediately closed it or stopped responding.

R means the host refused the initial request. T means it did not complete the Initial Connection Protocol and open a connection within 60 seconds. A mark identifies sites that said their systems might not be available at those times.
sections.plainLanguage: Each letter describes one connection test. The codes distinguish an accessible host from one that was unreachable, timed out, refused a connection or only partly opened it.

sections.title: Operator Status and Replacement
sections.content:
A separate table records site operators' status or predictions for hosts. Entries include Server, User only, Soon and expected dates, with a source person named for many predictions.

The unit metadata records RFC 319 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 315.
sections.plainLanguage: The report includes what site operators said about each host's role or expected readiness. RFC 319 later replaced it.
